desc:
A row of dominoes is a string of the characters L, R and .. A domino L has been pushed to the left, R to the right, and . is a domino still standing.

Every second, a falling domino pushes the standing neighbour in its falling direction: an R pushes the domino to its right, an L pushes the domino to its left. A standing domino that is pushed from both sides in the same second stays standing (the forces cancel). A domino that has fallen never changes again, and a falling domino only pushes a domino that is still standing.

Return the final state when nothing changes any more.

For example, "..R...L.." becomes "..RR.LL.."; ".L.R." becomes "LL.RR"; "R.L" stays "R.L".
constraints: dominoes contains only the characters L, R and .
hints: Simulating second by second works but can take O(n) rounds of O(n) work. Look at the row as segments between pushed dominoes.
Add a virtual L at the start and a virtual R at the end of the row; they never change the result but remove special cases. Then look at each pair of consecutive non-dot symbols.

For a pair of neighbours with dots between them: R...L meets in the middle (the middle dot stays if the count is odd), L...R leaves the dots standing, and equal symbols R...R or L...L fill all dots with that symbol.
editorial: Only the nearest pushed domino on each side of a standing domino matters. Scan the string with a pointer prev on the last pushed domino and a pointer i on the next one, with a virtual L in front and a virtual R at the end. The dots strictly between fall in four possible ways: both ends equal means they all fall that way; L then R means they all stay standing since the forces point away; R then L means the left half falls right, the right half falls left, and a single middle dot (odd count) stays up because both forces reach it in the same second.

The virtual ends keep the rule uniform: a leading R after the virtual L gives L-then-R (dots stay, but there are none before it), and a trailing L followed by the virtual R leaves nothing to push. The scan is linear in the length: O(n) time and O(n) space for the output array.
